ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ص وَالْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ (١) بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي عِزَّةٍ وَشِقَاقٍ (٢) كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ فَنَادَوْا وَلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ (٣)).
The majority read the dāl [Translator's note: i.e. the final dāl of the letter-name صَادْ] with a sukūn; its explanation has already been given.
It has been read with a kasra on it [Translator's note: i.e. صَادِ]. There are two views on it. The first: it is the kasra for the meeting of two sukūns. The second: it is an imperative from صَادَى; صَادَى الشَّيْءَ means: he faced it and matched it, i.e. "match the Qurʾān with your deeds."
It is also read with a fatḥa, i.e. "recite Ṣād" (اتْلُ صَادَ). And it has been said: it was given a vowel because of the meeting of two sukūns.
And (الْقُرْآنُ) is an oath. It has been said: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the oath, which is صَادْ.
As for the answer to the oath, it is omitted, i.e. "the truth has certainly come to you" (لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْحَقُّ), and the like. It has been said: it is the meaning of:
(بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا), i.e. "By the truth of the Qurʾān, the disbelievers have certainly opposed and been too proud for faith."
It has been said: the answer is «كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا», with the lām omitted, i.e. "how many indeed We destroyed" (لَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا); this is far-fetched, because كَمْ is in the position of an accusative by أَهْلَكْنَا. And it has been said: it is the meaning of this clause, i.e. "We have certainly destroyed many generations."
It has been said: it is His saying [the Exalted]: (إِنْ كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ). And it has been said: it is His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ); but between them there is long speech that prevents it from being the answer.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ): the origin is «لَا», to which the tāʾ was added, just as it was added to رُبَّ and ثُمَّ, so that one says رُبَّتَ and ثُمَّتْ.
Most of the Arabs give this tāʾ a fatḥa. As for the pause, some of them pause with the tāʾ, because particles are not a place for change, and some with the hāʾ, as one pauses on قَائِمَة.
As for «حِينَ», the doctrine of Sībawayh is that it is the khabar (predicate) of لَاتَ and its noun (ism) is omitted, because it operates as لَيْسَ does, i.e. "the time is not a time of flight" (لَيْسَ الْحِينُ حِينَ هَرَبٍ). One may not say that it [the noun] is latent (muḍmar), because pronouns are not latent in particles.
Al-Akhfash said: it is the one that operates in the chapter of negation [Translator's note: i.e. the lā of generic negation], so حِين is its noun and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "there is no time of escape for them" (لَا حِينَ مُنَاظِرٌ لَهُمْ) [Translator's note: so in the source; probably مَنَاصٍ is meant], or "[no such] time of theirs" (حِينُهُمْ).
Some of them put what follows it in the nominative and imply an accusative khabar, as one of them said:
فَأَنَا ابْنُ قَيْسٍ لَا بَرَاحُ
("For I am the son of Qays — there is no leaving [the field].")
Abū ʿUbayd said: the tāʾ is joined to حِين, not to لَا; he reported that they say تَحِين and تَلَان.
Some permitted the genitive after «لَاتَ», and cited verses for it; I have dealt with this exhaustively in ʿIlal al-Iʿrāb al-Kabīr.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا وَاصْبِرُوا عَلَى آلِهَتِكُمْ إِنَّ هَذَا لَشَيْءٌ يُرَادُ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنِ امْشُوا), i.e. "walk on" (امْشُوا) [Translator's note: i.e. أَنْ is explicative], because the meaning is: they set off in speech.
It has been said: it is setting off in the literal sense, and the implied form is: "and they set off saying: Walk on" (وَانْطَلَقُوا قَائِلِينَ: امْشُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ لَهُمْ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَلْيَرْتَقُوا فِي الْأَسْبَابِ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلْيَرْتَقُوا): this is speech construed according to the meaning, i.e. "if they claim that, then let them ascend."

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (جُنْدٌ مَا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جُنْدٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida), «هُنَالِكَ» is a naʿt (adjective), and «مَهْزُومٌ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also permissible that «هُنَالِكَ» be an adverbial (ẓarf) for مَهْزُوم.
And (مِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ) may be a naʿt of جُنْد, or be attached (mutaʿalliq) to مَهْزُوم, or be a naʿt of مَهْزُوم.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ وَأَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ أُولَئِكَ الْأَحْزَابُ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُولَئِكَ الْأَحْزَابُ): it may be resumptive; or it may be a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is from His saying (وَعَادٌ), or from «ثَمُودُ», or from His saying, Exalted is He: «وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا يَنْظُرُ هَؤُلَاءِ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً مَا لَهَا مِنْ فَوَاقٍ (١٥)).
And الْفَوَاق, with a ḍamma and with a fatḥa, are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both.

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُدَ ذَا الْأَيْدِ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (١٧) إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبَالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِشْرَاقِ (١٨)).
And (دَاوُدَ) is a badal (substitute).
And (سَخَّرْنَا) has been dealt with in al-Anbiyāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:21-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ نَبَأُ الْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرَابَ (٢١) إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَى دَاوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ خَصْمَانِ بَغَى بَعْضُنَا عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَاهْدِنَا إِلَى سَوَاءِ الصِّرَاطِ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْخَصْمُ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description; that is why it is neither put in the dual nor in the plural.
The first (إِذْ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for نَبَأ, and the second is a badal (substitute) from it, or an adverbial for «تَسَوَّرُوا». The pronoun is put in the plural though in reality it refers to two, by way of extended usage, because two is a plurality; His saying, Exalted is He, «خَصْمَانِ» indicates this, the implied form being "we are two disputants" (نَحْنُ خَصْمَانِ).

ukberi-tibyan:23-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَذَا أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً وَلِيَ نَعْجَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ (٢٣) قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَى نِعَاجِهِ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْخُلَطَاءِ لَيَبْغِي بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ وَظَنَّ دَاوُدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّاهُ فَاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًا وَأَنَابَ (٢٤) فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعَزَّنِي): with the doubled consonant, i.e. "he overcame me" (غَلَبَنِي).
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with the undoubled consonant, and the meaning is the same. It has been said: it is from وَعِزَ بِكَذَا, when one commands something; this is far-fetched, because before it there is a verb to which this would be conjoined — so some have stated.
It is also possible that the verb of saying has been omitted, i.e. "so he said: Entrust her to me; and he said: and he overcame me in speech."
And (سُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its direct object.
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): an exception from the same genus, and what it is excepted from is بَعْضُهُمْ; «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida), «هُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «قَلِيلٌ» is its khabar (predicate). It has been said: the implied form is "and they are few among them" (وَهُمْ قَلِيلٌ مِنْهُمْ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَنَّاهُ): with a doubled nūn, attributing the verb to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and with an undoubled one [Translator's note: i.e. فَتَنَاهُ], attributing it to the two angels.
(رَاكِعًا): an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) . . . [Translator's note: the ellipsis is in the source.]
And (ذَلِكَ) is the object of «غَفَرْنَا». It has been said: it is the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that" (الْأَمْرُ ذَلِكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا دَاوُدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ الْهَوَى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا نَسُوا يَوْمَ الْحِسَابِ (٢٤)) [Translator's note: so numbered in the source; this verse is 38:26].
(فَيُضِلَّكَ): accusative as the answer [to the prohibition]. It has been said: it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the prohibition, and the lām was given a fatḥa because of the meeting of two sukūns.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَاطِلًا ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النَّارِ (٢٧)).
And (بَاطِلًا) has been dealt with in Āl ʿImrān; and «أَمْ» in the two places [Translator's note: in the following verse, 28] is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa).

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٢٩)).
And (كِتَابٌ), i.e. "this is a Book" (هَذَا كِتَابٌ); and «مُبَارَكٌ» is another adjective (ṣifa).

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُدَ سُلَيْمَانَ نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (٣٠)).
(نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ), i.e. Sulaymān; and it has been said: Dāwūd. So the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted; and likewise in the story of Ayyūb.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ الصَّافِنَاتُ الْجِيَادُ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ عُرِضَ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for أَوَّاب; or its governor may be «نِعْمَ»; or the implied form may be "remember" (اذْكُرْ).
And (الْجِيَادُ) is the plural of جَوَاد; and it has been said: of جَيِّد.

ukberi-tibyan:32-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّى تَوَارَتْ بِالْحِجَابِ (٣٢) رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًا بِالسُّوقِ وَالْأَعْنَاقِ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ): it is the object of أَحْبَبْتُ, because the meaning of أَحْبَبْتُ is "I preferred" (آثَرْتُ); [it is not taken as its maṣdar] because the maṣdar of أَحْبَبْتُ is الْإِحْبَاب.
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) with its augment omitted.
Abū ʿAlī said: أَحْبَبْتُ has the meaning of "I sat down", from إِحْبَاب of the camel, which is its kneeling down.
And «حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ» is then a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), annexed to its object.
And (ذِكْرِ رَبِّي): it too is annexed to the object [Translator's note: i.e. "from my remembering my Lord"]. It has been said: to the agent, i.e. "from my Lord's remembering me" (عَنْ أَنْ يَذْكُرَنِي رَبِّي).
The fāʿil (agent) of «تَوَارَتْ» is the sun; it has not been mentioned, but the situation indicates it.
It has been said: the mention of الْإِشْرَاق (sunrise) in the story of Dāwūd, peace be upon him, indicates it.
And (رُدُّوهَا): the pronoun refers to the horses (الْجِيَاد).
And (مَسْحًا) is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has been said: the implied form is "stroking with a stroking" (يَمْسَحُ مَسْحًا).

ukberi-tibyan:34-37.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ (٣٤) قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ (٣٥) فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَاءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ (٣٦) وَالشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ (٣٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَسَدًا): it is the object of «أَلْقَيْنَا». It has been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from an omitted object, i.e. "We cast him"; it has been said: Sulaymān; and it has been said: his child, according to what has come in the exegesis (tafsīr).
And (تَجْرِي) is a ḥāl from الرِّيح.
And (رُخَاءً) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَجْرِي, i.e. "gentle" (لَيِّنَةً).
And (حَيْثُ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for تَجْرِي; and it has been said: for سَخَّرْنَا.
And (الشَّيَاطِينَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الرِّيح, and «كُلَّ» is a badal (substitute) from them.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ): it has been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «امْنُنْ» or in «أَمْسِكْ», the meaning being "without being called to account" (غَيْرَ مُحَاسَبٍ).
It has been said: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to عَطَاؤُنَا.
And it has been said: it is a ḥāl from it, i.e. "this is Our gift, abundant" (هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا وَاسِعًا), because الْحِسَاب has the meaning of "sufficient" (الْكَافِي).

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى): [«زُلْفَى»] is the noun (ism) of إِنَّ, and the khabar (predicate) is «لَهُ»; and what governs «عِنْدَ» is the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِنُصْبٍ): there are readings of it close in meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَذِكْرَى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ (٤٣)).
And (رَحْمَةً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصَارِ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عِبَادَنَا): it is read in the plural, and the names after it are a badal (substitute) from it; and in the singular [Translator's note: i.e. عَبْدَنَا], in which case «إِبْرَاهِيمَ» is a badal from it and what follows is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عَبْدَنَا.
It may also be a generic noun with the meaning of a plural, so that it is like the first reading.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِخَالِصَةٍ): it is read with annexation (iḍāfa) [Translator's note: i.e. بِخَالِصَةِ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ]; here it belongs to the category of annexing a thing to what clarifies it, because الْخَالِصَة may be a remembrance or something other than a remembrance.
And (ذِكْرَى) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «خَالِصَةٍ» is also a maṣdar with the meaning of الْإِخْلَاص (making pure), like الْعَافِيَة.
It has been said: «خَالِصَةٍ» is a maṣdar annexed to its object, i.e. "by their making pure the remembrance of the Abode" (بِإِخْلَاصِهِمْ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ). And it has been said: «خَالِصَةٍ» has the meaning of خُلُوص (being pure), so it is annexed to its agent, i.e. "in that the remembrance of the Abode was purely theirs" (بِأَنْ خَلَصَتْ لَهُمْ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ).
It has been said: «خَالِصَةٍ» is an active participle, its implied form being "by a pure [quality], the remembrance of the Abode" (بِخَالِصٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ), i.e. pure from being mixed with anything else.
It has been read with tanwīn on «خَالِصَةٍ»; then «ذِكْرَى» may be a badal (substitute) from it; or be in the position of an accusative as the object of خَالِصَة, or by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean); or be in the position of a nominative as the agent of «خَالِصَة», or on the implied form "it is a remembrance" (هِيَ ذِكْرَى).
As for the annexation of «ذِكْرَى» to «الدَّارِ», it is the annexation of the maṣdar to its object, i.e. "by their remembering the Abode of the Hereafter."
It has been said: in meaning it is an adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "their being remembered in the abode of this world"; so it is either a direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), as in "O thief of the night" (يَا سَارِقَ اللَّيْلَةِ), or by omission of the preposition, as in "I went [to] Syria" (ذَهَبْتُ الشَّامَ).

ukberi-tibyan:49-50.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (٤٩) جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوَابُ (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ): it is a badal (substitute) from «حُسْنَ مَآبٍ».
And (مُفَتَّحَةً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جَنَّات, according to those who make it definite by its annexation to عَدْن, which is a proper name, as they said "the Garden of Eternity" (جَنَّةُ الْخُلْدِ) and "the Garden of Refuge" (جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى).
Others said: it is indefinite, the meaning being "gardens of residence", so «مُفَتَّحَةً» is an adjective.
As for the nominative of (الْأَبْوَابُ), there are three views on it. The first: it is the fāʿil (agent) of «مُفَتَّحَةً» [Translator's note: i.e. in effect its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), مُفَتَّحَة being a passive participle], and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "with the gates of them opened for them" (مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوَابُ مِنْهَا); it was omitted as it was omitted in His saying: (فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى), i.e. "for them". The second: it is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in (مُفَتَّحَةً), which is the pronoun of the gardens; and «الْأَبْوَابُ» is not foreign to them, because they are part of the garden: you say "the garden was opened" meaning its gates; and of this kind is: (وَفُتِحَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا).
The third: like the first, except that the alif and lām are a substitute for the returning hāʾ; this is the view of the Kufans, and it is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرَابٍ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُتَّكِئِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive [pronoun] in «لَهُمْ», and the governor is «مُفَتَّحَةً».
It may also be a ḥāl from «الْمُتَّقِينَ», because a report has been made about them before the ḥāl.
It has been said: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَدْعُونَ», and it has come before its governor.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الْحِسَابِ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا تُوعَدُونَ): with yāʾ, as third person, the pronoun referring to the God-fearing; and with tāʾ, the implied form being "and it was said to them: this is what you are promised", the meaning being: "this is what you were promised."

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ هَذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِنْ نَفَادٍ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَالَهُ مِنْ نَفَادٍ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرِّزْق, and the governor is the demonstrative, i.e. "this is Our provision, lasting" (إِنَّ هَذَا لَرِزْقُنَا بَاقِيًا).

ukberi-tibyan:55-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ (٥٥) جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ (٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا), i.e. "the matter is this" (الْأَمْرُ هَذَا). Then He began anew and said: «وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ».
And (جَهَنَّمَ) is a badal (substitute) from «شَرَّ».
And (يَصْلَوْنَهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the [notion of] being settled (al-istiqrār) in His saying, Exalted is He: «لِلطَّاغِينَ».
It has been said: the implied form is "they will burn in Jahannam" (يَصْلَوْنَ جَهَنَّمَ); the verb was omitted because what follows indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَذَا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on the khabar (predicate):
The first: (فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ), as in your saying "Zayd — strike him" (زَيْدٌ اضْرِبْهُ).
Some said: this is weak because of the fāʾ, since it does not have the sense of an answer, like the one in His saying: (وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا). As for (حَمِيمٌ) on this view, it may be a badal (substitute) from هَذَا, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is scalding water" (هُوَ حَمِيمٌ), or a second khabar.
The second view: that (حَمِيمٌ) is the khabar of (هَذَا), with (فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ) parenthetical between them.
It has been said: هَذَا is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "let them taste this" (فَلْيَذُوقُوا هَذَا); then He began anew and said (حَمِيمٌ), i.e. "it is scalding water" (هُوَ حَمِيمٌ).
As for (غَسَّاقٌ), it is read with the doubled consonant, like كَفَّار and صَبَّار; and with the undoubled one [Translator's note: i.e. غَسَاقٌ] as a noun for the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "possessing darkness" (ذُو غَسَقٍ); or فَعَّال has the meaning of فَاعِل.

ukberi-tibyan:58-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْوَاجٌ (٥٨) هَذَا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ لَا مَرْحَبًا بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صَالُوا النَّارِ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآخَرُ): it is read in the plural [Translator's note: i.e. وَأُخَرُ], and there are two views on it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
«مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it, i.e. "of the kind of the scalding water", and «أَزْوَاجٌ» is its khabar (predicate).
The second: the khabar is omitted, i.e. "and they have other [kinds]" (وَلَهُمْ أُخَرُ), and «مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» and «أَزْوَاجٌ» are two adjectives.
It is also permissible that «مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» be an adjective and «أَزْوَاجٌ» be put in the nominative by the preposition-phrase.
The pronoun is masculine because the meaning is "of the kind of what we have mentioned."
It is also read in the singular [Translator's note: i.e. وَآخَرُ], conjoined (maʿṭūf) to حَمِيم; «مِنْ شَكْلِهِ» is a naʿt of it, and «أَزْوَاجٌ» is put in the nominative by the preposition-phrase.
It may also be nominative on the implied form "it is", i.e. the scalding water.
And the other kind is His saying, Exalted is He: (مُقْتَحِمٌ), i.e. [rushing into] the Fire [Translator's note: so in the source].
And (مَعَكُمْ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مُقْتَحِمٌ, or from (فَوْجٌ), because it has been qualified; it may not be an adverbial (ẓarf), because the meaning would be corrupted. It may also be a second naʿt.
And (لَا مَرْحَبًا): it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, i.e. "this is a troop to whom it is said: No welcome" (هَذَا فَوْجٌ مَقُولًا لَهُ: لَا مَرْحَبًا).
And مَرْحَبًا is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or as a direct object, i.e. "they do not hear [a] welcome" (لَا يَسْمَعُونَ مَرْحَبًا).

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا رَبَّنَا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا فِي النَّارِ (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ قَدَّمَ): it has the meaning of الَّذِي, and «فَزِدْهُ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also permissible that «مَنْ» be accusative, i.e. "so increase whoever brought forward…" (فَزِدْ مَنْ قَدَّمَ).
It has been said: it is an interrogative expressing magnification; so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and قَدَّمَ is the khabar, and then a new sentence begins; there is weakness in this.
And (ضِعْفًا) is a naʿt (adjective) of عَذَاب, i.e. "doubled" (مُضَاعَفًا).
And (فِي النَّارِ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for زِدْ.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, i.e. "increase him while he is in the Fire" (زِدْهُ كَائِنًا فِي النَّارِ); or a second naʿt of عَذَاب; or a ḥāl [from it], because it has been qualified.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصَارُ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ): it is read with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ), because it is for the interrogative; and with the connecting one (waṣl), on the omission of the interrogative particle, because أَمْ indicates it. It has been said: the first [i.e. the clause on this reading] is a statement, and is in meaning an adjective of رِجَال [Translator's note: in the preceding verse, مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَى رِجَالًا]; and «أَمْ» is interrogative, i.e. "are they missing, or have [the eyes] turned aside?" (أَهُمْ مَفْقُودُونَ أَمْ زَاغَتْ).
And (سِخْرِيًّا) has been dealt with in «al-Muʾminūn».

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ): it is a badal (substitute) from «حَقٌّ», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the disputing" (هُوَ تَخَاصُمٌ).
If it were said that it is nominative by حَقّ [Translator's note: i.e. as its agent], that would be far-fetched, because it would then become a clause with no pronoun in it referring back to the noun of «إِنَّ».

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or an adjective (ṣifa); or a badal (substitute); or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «الْعَزِيزُ».

ukberi-tibyan:69-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِالْمَلَأِ الْأَعْلَى إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ (٦٩) إِنْ يُوحَى إِلَيَّ إِلَّا أَنَّمَا أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ): it is an adverbial (ẓarf) for عِلْم.
And (أَنَّمَا) is nominative by يُوحَى إِلَيَّ [Translator's note: i.e. as its deputy agent].
It has been said: «إِلَيَّ» stands in the place of the fāʿil (agent), and إنما [Translator's note: so in the source; أَنَّمَا is meant] is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "the warning was revealed to me" (أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ الْإِنْذَارُ), or "that I am a warner" (بِأَنِّي نَذِيرٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَرًا مِنْ طِينٍ (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ), i.e. "remember when He said" (اذْكُرْ إِذْ قَالَ).
(مِنْ طِينٍ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of بَشَر, or be attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَالِق.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَالْحَقُّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ (٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَالْحَقُّ) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the discussion is of the accusative reading فَالْحَقَّ]: there are two views on its accusative. The first: it is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "so establish the truth" (فَأَحِقَّ الْحَقَّ), or "so mention the truth" (فَاذْكُرِ الْحَقَّ). The second: on the implied omission of the oath, i.e. "so by the truth, I will surely fill" (فَبِالْحَقِّ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ).
(وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ) is then parenthetical between them. Sībawayh rejects that, because it [Translator's note: the preposition of the oath] may not be omitted except with the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
It is also read in the nominative, i.e. "for I am the Truth" (فَأَنَا الْحَقُّ), or "for the truth is from Me" (فَالْحَقُّ مِنِّي).
As for the second «الْحَقُّ», its accusative is by أَقُولُ. It is [also] read [in the nominative], on the implied repetition of the nominative before it, or by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "my saying is the truth" (قَوْلِي الْحَقُّ); on this view «أَقُولُ» is resumptive and joined to what follows it, i.e. "I say: I will surely fill" (أَقُولُ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ).
It has been said: «أَقُولُ» is a khabar (predicate) about it, with the hāʾ omitted, i.e. "I say it" (أَقُولُهُ); this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينٍ (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ), i.e. "you will surely know" (لَتَعْرِفُنَّ); it has one object, which is «نَبَأَهُ». It may also be transitive to two objects, the second being «بَعْدَ حِينٍ».
